snapshot.summary: Haiti's new election timetable was reported amid a foreign security deployment. Christine Lagarde announced an early ECB departure. The UN again opposed the Cuba embargo, although support fell.
connections: Editorial connection: domestic political legitimacy, international financial governance and economic coercion each involved institutions whose announcements did not settle their practical effects.
uncertainties: Haiti's security and electoral readiness, the ECB succession and the practical effect of the Cuba vote remained open.

stories.title: UN again calls for ending Cuba's embargo as support declines
stories.summary: The General Assembly's October 28 resolution passed by 130 votes to 17, with 25 abstentions. Reporting contrasted Washington's success in shifting votes with the continuing majority against the embargo and its sovereignty implications.
stories.whyItMatters: The vote tests international support for economic pressure on Cuba, while offering no direct mechanism to remove US restrictions.
stories.selectionRationale: A major multilateral vote receiving fresh October 29 coverage, with consequences for economic coercion and diplomatic alignment.
